feature_candidates.expected_impact: High; tab alone has large rate differences, hour may add recency/fatigue effects.

feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; tab and hour are observed at exposure time, no future info.

feature_candidates.description: Train-only prefix-computed rate of user's past long_view per video category (or tag), updated per exposure.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Moderate; captures user preferences and may improve ranking within user.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute on-the-fly during training using train-only interactions; store per-user, per-category counters.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: High if computed over full log; must be strictly prefix (only prior exposures) to avoid future leakage.
feature_candidates.name: user_history_longview_rate_per_category

feature_candidates.description: Use is_like, is_comment, is_forward as auxiliary targets in a multi-task loss to sharpen long_view representation.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Moderate; auxiliary labels share user intent and could regularize the main objective.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add auxiliary heads and combine losses; available labels in train; no change to primary label.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; labels are contemporaneous with long_view and do not include future info.
feature_candidates.name: multi_task_auxiliary_labels

findings.evidence: DATA CARD tab breakdown (train) shows wide rate differences across tabs.
findings.implication: Including tab as a categorical feature (or per-tab user history) should improve ranking significantly.
findings.observation: Long_view rate varies dramatically by tab: tab 4 at 48.93%, tab 1 at 38.61%, tab 0 at 4.22% (train).
findings.title: Tab position is a strong categorical predictor

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Data Quality' section lists zero-duration and duplicate counts.
findings.implication: Univariate correlation analyses should exclude or flag these rows to avoid spurious estimates.
findings.observation: 239 videos with zero duration (24,076 rows) and 15,609 exact duplicate rows exist in train log.
findings.title: Data quality issues can bias correlations

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Rows per User' percentile and leakage risk note on user history features.
findings.implication: Build history features using only prior logged exposures per user to avoid future leakage.
findings.observation: Users have median 34 rows (p50), providing enough history for aggregates, but validation-period rows must be excluded from history computation.
findings.title: User history requires train-only prefix windows

expected_artifacts: video_feature_univariate_scores.txt (logistic regression coefficients, excluding leaky table initially).
eda_leakage_audit.md (documentation of any leaky table usage and mitigation decisions).
feature_hypotheses: Temporal features (hour, day-of-week, time since last exposure) and within-session position improve ranking due to recency and fatigue effects.
User historical long_view rate per tab and per video category (computed from train-only, prefixed windows) adds predictive signal for next exposure.
Video popularity from the leaky aggregate table (caveated with risk controls, e.g., min exposure count) can boost ranking without significant leakage if handled as a decaying feature.
Multi-task auxiliary labels (is_like, is_comment, is_forward) share latent user intent with long_view and can be exploited via a group_softmax or multi_task family without changing the primary label.
leakage_risks: Video statistics aggregate spans a period 45-181 days longer than the interaction log, leaking future popularity into past ranking decisions.
Duplicate rows (15,609) and zero-duration videos (239) may bias correlation estimates if not removed before aggregation.
User history features computed from the full log, including the validation period, would leak future responses into training; must be strictly train-only or prefix-split.
Position and tab variables are confounded with user intent; naive correlations can mislead without within-user stratification.
plan.objective: Plan a leakage-safe EDA pass on KuaiRand-Pure to identify feature families and preprocessing choices that could lift within-user long_view ranking above baseline 0.6016, focusing on registered families and the known constraints.
questions: How does long_view rate vary by hour, day-of-week, tab, and within-user exposure position, controlling for user fixed effects?
What is the association between user history aggregates (past long_view/click rates per tab or video category) and future long_view in train?
Which video attributes (e.g., tags, categories, duration) show the strongest univariate correlation with long_view, after removing zero-duration and duplicate rows?
Do auxiliary labels (like/comment/forward) at the user-item level correlate with long_view enough to justify multi-task auxiliary objectives?
required_inputs: Train and validation interaction logs (user_id, video_id, tab, position, timestamp/hour, all labels).
Video feature table and user profile table (for category/tag and user-level attributes).
Video statistics table (leaky) with explicit column names and observation period bounds.
Existing model config and candidate.py API from the current experiment family (bpr/group_softmax) to align feature engineering.

report.recommended_next_focus: Run a univariate logistic regression on cleaned train data (excluding leaky video stats) to confirm tab and hour effects, then implement tab interaction and prefix-based history features.
report.summary: EDA plan focuses on leakage-safe analysis of tab/hour/user-history features and multi-task auxiliary labels to lift within-user long_view ranking from 0.6016, using train-only aggregates and cleaning duplicate/zero-duration rows.
ui_notes: Tab 4 (48.93% long_view) vs tab 0 (4.22%) is a huge gap; consider separate tab embeddings.
Remove zero-duration and duplicate rows before any correlation analysis to avoid bias.
Do not use the leaky video stats table until designing a decaying popularity feature with exposure-count controls.
